operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Fixed glyph, changing world". Objective: Make a memorable product promise through a consistent visual anchor. Visual rule: The anchor never changes position or silhouette while the world around it changes. Beats, in order: - 0–1.5 s: One large glyph/icon and a short premise. Shows Brand color, Anchor glyph, Premise. - 1.5–4.5 s: Two worlds appear around the same anchor. Shows Brand color, World 1, Anchor glyph, Label for worlds 1 and 2. - 4.5–7.5 s: Two more worlds expand the range. Shows Brand color, World 2, Anchor glyph, Label for worlds 1 and 2. - 7.5–9.5 s: Worlds clear to reveal the concrete promise. Shows Brand color, World 3, Anchor glyph, Label for worlds 3 and 4. - 9.5–12 s: Anchor becomes part of the brand/CTA lockup. Shows Brand color, World 4, Anchor glyph, Label for worlds 3 and 4. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: premise (Premise: anchor, at most 7 words); label12 (Label for worlds 1 and 2: worlds 1, at most 7 words); label34 (Label for worlds 3 and 4: worlds 2, at most 7 words); promise (Promise: promise, at most 7 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: glyph (Anchor glyph: An icon or mark on a plain or transparent background. It shows small, as a node or tile, so it must read at about 200 px wide. Not a screenshot or a social preview card. Shown in: One large glyph/icon and a short premise. | Two worlds appear around the same anchor. | Two worlds appear around the same anchor. | Two more worlds expand the range. | Two more worlds expand the range. | Worlds clear to reveal the concrete promise. | Anchor becomes part of the brand/CTA lockup.); world1 (World 1: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Two worlds appear around the same anchor.); world2 (World 2: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Two worlds appear around the same anchor.); world3 (World 3: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Two more worlds expand the range.); world4 (World 4: A real photo or screenshot that matches the beats that show it. Shown in: Two more worlds expand the range.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Anchor becomes part of the brand/CTA lockup.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
